clue.text: Mark time digging into what got Socrates started?

indicators.note: the time letter burrows inside the Greek letter's name, so one goes within the other

parts.note: Socrates begins with S, and in his own Greek that letter is sigma

explanation.surface: A philosophy student marks the moment that set Socrates thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the trick: Socrates' first letter is wanted as he would have written it, the Greek sigma, and T goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a mark of disgrace, and in botany or medicine also a spot or visible mark.

clue.text: One not wanted on IT list

definitions.text: One not wanted on IT list

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece sits on top of the other, so the T comes first
the one is unwanted, so it is taken away from the letters of IT

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral
a roll is a list of names, as in a register

explanation.surface: Someone unwelcome on a mailing list for computer staff.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: remove I from IT to leave T, place it on ROLL, and the result is the person nobody wants in an online forum.
explanation.definitionFit: An internet troll posts provocative messages to upset others, so is unwelcome on any online list or forum.

clue.text: Legendary giant among British compilers polled future leading lights?

parts.note: Gog, with Magog, is a giant of British legend, the guardian of the City of London

indicators.note: polled means with the head cut off, so the first letter goes

parts.note: crossword compilers are setters

explanation.surface: Crossword setters were surveyed on who will become the stars of tomorrow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polled' looks like 'surveyed' but means beheaded, as with a polled tree or hornless cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: Go-getters are ambitious, energetic people likely to become prominent figures later on.

clue.text: Paris Fashion: who transfixes in the style of stars?

indicators.note: to transfix is to pierce through, so the French word runs through the middle of the other phrase

parts.note: à la, borrowed from French, means in the style of
'who' in the Paris fashion, that is in French, is qui

explanation.surface: A query about which Paris designer dresses people like celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion' suggests the catwalk, but 'Paris Fashion' only tells you to put 'who' into French.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquila, the Eagle, is a constellation, a named group of stars in the northern sky.

clue.text: Books confiscated by Twitter billionaire after review

indicators.note: review is read here as looking back, so the held letters are taken in the opposite direction
the letters are held, as if seized, by the words that follow

explanation.surface: Books seized by a social-media tycoon after he looked them over.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside 'twITTER BILlionaire' read right to left: LIBRETTI.
explanation.definitionFit: A libretto is the text of an opera, commonly called its book, so libretti are books.

clue.text: It hurt bores did a number on buddy after upsetting drink

indicators.note: in a down answer, on means placed below, so the singing phrase goes under the buddy word
the performed number comes after the buddy word in the answer
in a down answer, upsetting turns the word on its head, so it reads from the bottom up

parts.note: a pal is a buddy

indicators.note: the cry bores into the middle of the singing phrase

parts.note: to do a number is to perform a piece of music: sang song
ouch is what you say when it hurts

explanation.surface: An odd scene of pain, boredom and a song performed for a friend after a spilt drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Did a number' means performed a song, sang song, not hurt someone; 'upsetting' turns the buddy word upside down, as this is a down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lapsang souchong is a smoky Chinese black tea, so a drink.

clue.text: Times keeps moving around a third anniversary

indicators.note: the multiplication word keeps the shuffled letters inside it

parts.note: by means times in arithmetic, as in three by four

indicators.note: the letters of 'a third' are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: The Times newspaper is marking a third anniversary with some upheaval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper, but it is the multiplication word, as in three by four.
explanation.definitionFit: A birthday is the annual return of the day of someone's birth, an anniversary of it.

clue.text: Message not normal material but abstract art

indicators.note: the letters of material are put into an abnormal order
to abstract is to take away, so the letters of art are removed from the pool

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses some abstract art as unusual material that sends a message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abstract art' reads as a style of painting, but 'abstract' is a verb: take A, R, T out of MATERIAL and rearrange the remaining M, E, I, A, L.
explanation.definitionFit: An email is an electronic message sent between computers.

clue.text: Joe & co initially caught in limbo but conversely keeping up

indicators.note: the turned-round letters keep the word for up inside them
conversely means the other way round, so the letters are read backwards
initially takes the first letter of each of the next three words

parts.note: hep, an older form of hip, means up to date or well-informed, as in up on the news

explanation.surface: Joe and company get caught in a state of limbo but keep their spirits up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conversely' acts on the initials and 'but' together, and the up word goes in after the reversal. 'Joe & co' points to Joe Public, the ordinary person.
explanation.definitionFit: Joe Public is the typical ordinary citizen, so Joe and his kind make up the general population.

clue.text: Garment for one during a bad winter/one after a good spring

definitions.text: Garment for one during a bad winter
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a long knitted sweater, a jumper being a British word for a pullover, worn in harsh cold
second meaning: an athlete in the long jump, who needs a good leap to do well

explanation.walkthrough: The slash splits the clue into two halves; 'spring' looks like the season after winter, but it is the athlete's leap.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a sweater with extra length and a competitor in the long-jump athletics event.

clue.text: Doing a twirl, I'm sorry to interrupt 17's Dutch attention seeker

indicators.note: twirling spins the whole thing round so it reads backwards
the apology word breaks into the middle of the mother word

parts.note: 17 is MY OLD MAN, which also means pop, and pop's Dutch (Cockney slang for wife) is ma
eh? is what you say for 'I'm sorry, what did you say?'

explanation.surface: Someone twirling apologises for interrupting a Dutch woman seeking the limelight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch' is Cockney slang for wife, as in 'my old Dutch'; pop's wife is mum. The twirl reverses everything after the apology is put in.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahem is the little throat-clearing cough used to draw someone's attention.

clue.text: Many embarking make up a fleet

indicators.note: the many go aboard, entering the word for make up

parts.note: to fill a prescription is to make it up
a lot means many

explanation.surface: Lots of people boarding ships form a fleet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make up' sounds like inventing, but it is filling a prescription; 'embarking' suits the fleet in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A flotilla is a small fleet of boats or ships sailing together.

clue.text: Go to ground, just ahead of course!

definitions.meaning: second meaning: in golf match play, a player one hole ahead on the course is said to be one ...

explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' sounds like 'naturally', but it means on the golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: To hole up is to take refuge out of sight, and in golf it describes a narrow lead of one hole.

clue.text: Whom jungle-man to start afresh wants for wife?

definitions.text: Whom jungle-man to start afresh wants for wife?

indicators.note: to start means take just the first letter of the hyphenated word
wants means lacks here, so the word for afresh lacks its wife letter

parts.note: anew means afresh
W is the abbreviation for wife, used in genealogies

explanation.surface: Who would the jungle hero choose as a wife to begin life again?
explanation.walkthrough: The jungle-man is Tarzan; 'wants' looks like desire but means lacks, taking W out of ANEW.
explanation.definitionFit: In Edgar Rice Burroughs' stories Jane Porter becomes Tarzan's wife.

clue.text: Pronunciation of Hebrew while nurse is in hospital loo

parts.note: as can mean while, as in 'as I walked'
H is the standard map abbreviation for hospital

indicators.note: the nurse is in the toilet word, sitting inside it

parts.note: kazi is British slang for a toilet
EN is an enrolled nurse

explanation.surface: A nurse in a hospital toilet is heard pronouncing Hebrew.
explanation.walkthrough: Kazi is British slang for a lavatory; an enrolled nurse was a grade of nurse in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashkenazi Hebrew is the traditional pronunciation used by Jews of Central and Eastern European descent.

clue.text: Grand day to open fifty mayonnaise plants

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand pounds
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

indicators.note: the day letter opens up the sauce, going inside it

parts.note: aioli is a garlic mayonnaise

explanation.surface: A grand day out to launch fifty jars of mayonnaise among the plants.
explanation.walkthrough: D goes into AIOLI after its A, giving ADIOLI, after G and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladioli are tall flowering garden plants grown from corms, named for their sword-shaped leaves.

clue.text: Study image put together in it?

definitions.text: Study image put together in it?

indicators.note: these two pieces, put together, go inside the letters of it

parts.note: a den is a study, a private room for work
a tiki is a carved Polynesian figure or image

explanation.surface: Examine a picture that was assembled in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Study' looks like a verb but is a room; 'put together' joins the room and the carved figure before they go inside it, and the whole clue then describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An Identikit is a composite picture of a suspect assembled from separate facial features.

clue.text: Pop song?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a name for one's father
second meaning: the music-hall song beginning '... said follow the van'

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop song' looks like one phrase for chart music, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for one's father is also the title of a famous music-hall number by Marie Lloyd.

clue.text: Authority? These days editor, getting ignored, has none

indicators.note: the editor is ignored, so those letters are left out

parts.note: taken as written
O is zero, none

explanation.surface: A complaint that editors are ignored these days and have no authority.
explanation.walkthrough: The editor is removed from inside the phrase, not from its end, and the zero for 'none' is added after.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's say-so is their permission or authorisation, the power to decide.

clue.text: Stylet chaser has taken to?

indicators.note: the run of letters is taken up within the two words that come first

explanation.surface: What has an engraver with a fine point taken up?
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'stylET CHaser'; and a chaser, who decorates metal, with a stylet is just the person to engrave.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to engrave a design into metal, the work a metal chaser does with a pointed tool.

clue.text: Sign one of my books? He's forgotten

indicators.note: these letters are forgotten, so dropped from the book

parts.note: a setter's book is a thesaurus
the letters of he's, minus the apostrophe

explanation.surface: An author asks a reader to sign a copy, but the man has forgotten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' is the setter, whose working book is a thesaurus; take out H, E, S to leave T and AURUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Taurus, the Bull, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: My chauffeur and I fib about clipping nose of Volkswagen Beetle

parts.note: the chauffeur and I together are we

indicators.note: the word for fib clips around the letter, holding it inside
about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a fib is a lie

indicators.note: the nose is the front, the first letter of the car name

explanation.surface: Someone and their chauffeur lie about scraping the front of a VW Beetle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beetle' looks like the car, but it is the insect. LIE reversed is EIL, and V goes in after the first E.
explanation.definitionFit: A weevil is a small beetle with a long snout that damages grain and crops.

clue.text: Particular about fare for one boarding what 17 suggests we follow

indicators.note: the example word boards the vehicle, going inside it

parts.note: the song at 17, My Old Man, goes 'My old man said follow the van'
eg, for example, means for one

explanation.surface: A fussy eater on board the removal van the song tells us to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: The music-hall song 'My Old Man' opens 'My old man said follow the van', so the vehicle is a VAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A vegan is strict about food, eating nothing from animals, so is choosy about what they eat.

clue.text: Wearing my old university hat loony grabs my partner?

indicators.note: the exclamation wears the jumbled letters, covering them like clothing
the exclamation grabs the jumbled letters, holding them inside

parts.note: cor! is an exclamation of surprise, like my!

indicators.note: loony means crazy, so the university and hat letters are jumbled

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for university, followed by hat as written

explanation.surface: A lunatic in an old college hat grabs someone's partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' looks like a possessive, but it is the exclamation cor!, which takes the jumble inside it. 'My partner' fits a setter, whose partner in writing shares the byline.
explanation.definitionFit: A co-author writes a book jointly with another writer, so is a writing partner.

clue.text: Shabby Scottish messenger is out of credit

indicators.note: the credit letters go out of the messenger word, leaving the rest

parts.note: a courier is a messenger
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: A shabby Scottish courier has run out of money.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the C and the R from COURIER to leave OURIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ourie is a Scots dialect word meaning dingy, drab or dismal in appearance.

clue.text: Part of an Indian legend with a final twist?

indicators.note: the ending is twisted, so near the end one letter changes place

parts.note: a saga is a legend or long heroic story

explanation.surface: A query about a piece of an Indian legend with a surprise ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'An Indian' means an Indian meal, as in 'going for an Indian'. In SAGA the G moves past the final A.
explanation.definitionFit: Saag is a spinach curry dish served as part of an Indian restaurant meal.

clue.text: Why is one of these southerners mistaken for Yorkshirewoman?

indicators.note: one of the southerners, with WHY IS, is jumbled and mistaken for the northern woman

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
these turns the single 'one' into the whole group, the plural ending

explanation.surface: Why is a southerner taken for a woman from Yorkshire?
explanation.walkthrough: WHY IS plus one of the southerners has exactly the letters of YORKSHIREWOMAN. Moonrakers are people from Wiltshire, a county in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonraker is the folk nickname for natives of Wiltshire, from smugglers who claimed to be raking the moon.

clue.text: Sadly ignorant folk will find bliss here

indicators.note: sadly means in a sorry state, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A twist on 'ignorance is bliss': the ignorant will find happiness here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Folk' hints at folklore: Tír na nÓg is the Irish land of eternal youth.
explanation.definitionFit: Tír na nÓg is the Otherworld of Irish mythology, a paradise of everlasting youth and joy.

clue.text: Info soldiers conveyed with it?

indicators.note: the info word conveys the other pieces, carrying them inside

parts.note: SP, starting price, is British slang for the information, as in 'what's the SP?'
RE is the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: News passed to the troops along with the kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'SP' as slang for the lowdown comes from horse racing's starting price; the Royal Engineers are the usual crossword soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitrep, situation report, is a military update on current conditions given to soldiers.
